advisory.finding: _trusted_remote ignores -c CLI overrides (config._CLI_OVERRIDES) when it resolves sync.remote. The remote that picks the base is drawn from a different set of layers than the gate config it then builds, which does include the cli layer. With `rebar -c sync.remote=upstream verify-opcert`, the gate silently reads origin's base while the reported config says sync.remote=upstream.

advisory.suggested_fix: In _trusted_remote, after the env layer add `if config._CLI_OVERRIDES: layers.append(coerce_sparse(config._CLI_OVERRIDES, source="cli", strict=strict))`.

advisory.suggested_fix: Have base_ref return (ref, remote), or let gate_config resolve the remote once, and thread `remote` through _reviewed_project and _hop_target. Use it to build the prefix and the fetch hint.

advisory.finding: `verify-opcert` now reads the base branch's committed `[snapshot].ref` and exits 2 on values the shared gate-ref resolver still accepts as valid: `HEAD`, a commit SHA, `refs/heads/<branch>`, or a branch on a different remote (`upstream/main` when the gate remote is `origin`). Before this change `verify-opcert` ignored `[snapshot].ref` completely. A repository that already commits one of these documented values to its default branch, for the LLM gates' `--ref` default, will now see its op-cert merge gate fail.
scenarios: A downstream repo commits `[snapshot]\nref = "refs/heads/main"` or a release tag so that review-plan, scan-spec and verify-completion read a fixed ref. After upgrading rebar, every verify-opcert CI run exits 2 even though the trust configuration did not change.
A repo whose gates read `upstream/main` (`[snapshot].ref = "upstream/main"`) while CI's checkout remote is `origin` now fails the op-cert gate.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either accept `refs/heads/<branch>` (map it to `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`), or treat values that do not name a branch (HEAD, SHA, tag) as 'no hop' and print a stderr warning instead of raising ConfigError. Keep fail-closed only for a value that names a different remote. In either case, document the new constraint as a breaking change in the release notes.

dropped.finding: base_ref never checks the exit status of `git symbolic-ref --quiet refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`. 'No symref recorded' (rc 1), 'a direct, non-symbolic HEAD ref', and a fatal git error (rc 128) all look the same, and each falls back to <remote>/main without a message. In a repo whose default branch is not main but which still has a stale <remote>/main, a failed lookup reads the stale branch's trust config. If main is also missing, the error says it 'tried' <remote>/HEAD even though the lookup never ran.
scenarios: Default branch is trunk, a stale origin/main still exists locally, and symbolic-ref fails for an environmental reason: the gate reads main's old [verify] settings.
dropped.suggested_fix: `sym = _git(root, "symbolic-ref", "--quiet", tried[0]); if sym.returncode not in (0, 1): raise ConfigError(f"op-cert gate: git symbolic-ref {tried[0]} failed: {sym.stderr.strip()}"); head = sym.stdout.strip() if sym.returncode == 0 else ""`

src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:4 and :74: `[snapshot].ref` is documented as the code-reading gates' read `ref` (branch | tag | SHA, `REBAR_GATE_REF > [snapshot].ref > origin/main`). A repo may set it to something like `develop` or `release` for those gates without meaning to hand that branch the op-cert trust root

src/rebar/_opcert_gate_config.py:8-9: the module states its threat model as a change that could "drop `require_environment`, or point `tracker.dir` at an empty directory, and so loosen the gate that checks it"; the hop lets those same edits take effect through a branch other than the protected default branch
dropped.finding: The one-hop follow of the base's committed `[snapshot].ref` moves the op-cert gate's trusted project layer (`require_environment`, `opcert_enforce_since`, `tracker.dir`) from the remote's default branch to any branch of that remote. Nothing checks that the target branch is as protected as the base. If someone can push to that branch without review, they can drop `require_environment` or point `tracker.dir` at an empty store, and the gate stops checking op-certs for later changes.
scenarios: The default branch commits `[snapshot]\nref = "develop"` so the LLM gates read `develop`. A contributor with push access to `develop`, which has weaker branch protection than `main`, commits `[verify]` without `require_environment`, or with `tracker.dir` pointing at an empty directory. Every later `verify-opcert` run then reads that config and passes closed tickets that have no valid op-cert.

In a same-repo PR workflow, PR branches live on `origin`. If the base's `[snapshot].ref` names a shared branch that PR authors can push to, a PR author can change the gate config that applies to their own PR before it merges.
